in_use_evidence: At 2ed84b9 no Gherkin runner or parser reads gigacron.feature outside the run: .pre-commit-config.yaml runs only spec-lint, which the finding says misses the error, and no CI workflow or test code references the file. Stories ST-0002A/D/E trace DOM-04 but no option of the Fix changes them.
why: The Scenario uses the nonexistent Or keyword, so the official parser refuses the whole shared file and no Gherkin tool can read any Rule in it; no tool outside the run reads the syntax yet, so it is not in use.

in_use_evidence: At 7cd01b2 ST-0003B.md, ST-0003B-details.md, ST-0003D.md and ST-0003F.md only link to T-0051..T-0054 and defer to them; no option of the Fix (rewrite T-0052/53/54, fix the comment in state-machines.md) forces a change to any story or code, so they do not encode the statement.
why: T-0052, T-0053 and T-0054 describe a config_hash column, missing range columns and a required dispatch_target that the entity model contradicts, so a planning agent that cuts the Folder or claims stories builds the wrong schema.

in_use_evidence: At 7cd01b2 the delivered code (task_registry/routes.py::publish_task_drafts, ST-0003B/D) uses POST /publications, but neither option of the Fix changes that code or those stories: one rewrites the spec to match, the other only notes the code in the gaps report. None encodes the per-draft statement.
why: interface-contracts.md and the state machine define a per-draft publish route while DOM-03 code references and the delivered route define a batch route, so the next story that adds a publication check cannot tell which contract to build without asking the stakeholder.
rule_gap: In use, 'a story or code encodes the statement when an option of the Fix forces a change': the rule does not say what holds when delivered code already encodes the opposite of the spec text and the Fix is a stakeholder choice between two targets.

in_use_evidence: At 59b6757 the code (DefinitionStoreService._require_publishable_drafts, test_publication_routes.py:298) already answers with field-code problems; no option of the Fix forces a change to it (option 1 rewrites spec uses, option 2 only marks the form as delivered code T-0057 replaces). why: A nameless draft gets REQUIRED problems in interface-contracts.md and DEF-07 but TASK_DRAFT_INVALID in validation-rules.md, state-machines.md, FLD-08 and DEF-14, so the next publication story writes tests that contradict one of the two and must ask which form wins.
rule_gap: In use, same text as SPEC-0014: when the Fix is a choice between two targets, it does not say whether code that already follows one side counts as encoding the statement.

in_use_evidence: At 59b6757 packages/server/backend/src/gigacron_server/task_registry/services/definition_store_service.py::_require_publishable_drafts (line 310, delivered by ST-0003B on dev) returns one problem per field error, and tests/task_registry/test_publication_routes.py:316 asserts the REQUIRED pair; the Fix forces a change to both.
why: interface-contracts.md:207-209 contradicts three artifacts that state TASK_DRAFT_INVALID, and code on dev outside the run already follows the wrong paragraph, so clients may already receive the wrong refusal form.
rule_gap: harms_downstream in the document class says 'contradicts an accepted specification'; the finding does not show which side was accepted (DEC-54 says 'as ST-0003B delivered it'), so the rule leaves open whether code that follows the contested side is harm.

in_use_evidence: At bd9d718 ST-0003 has status pending and no publication code exists in packages/server/backend/src; no story or code outside the run encodes the Scenario.
why: The spec states a target Scenario whose story ST-0003 is still pending, and the scope map already shows DOM-03 as specified, so nothing is wrong and a reader acts correctly at the first reading.
rule_gap: Reconciliation kinds (code-defect, spec-stale, undocumented, speculative) and 'a defect means the artifact is wrong as it stands' do not say whether a target-state Scenario with a pending story is a defect or only information.
